newsitem.title: USA: US W. Coast crude market thin ahead of scheduling.
newsitem.headline: US W. Coast crude market thin ahead of scheduling.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crude buying was thin Tuesday, with most refiners supplied for June and waiting for pipeline scheduling to begin later this week, traders said.
In futures markets, June deliveries of West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude expired 40 below the previous session at $21.19 a barrel.
The benchmark West Coast grade, Alaska North Slope (ANS), tracked the fall in futures and spot markets.
Outright ANS prices fell 30 cents a barrel to $19.60/19.80 a barrel.
ANS discounts have remained flat at $1.50 a barrel under WTI, with BP, a leading seller, keeping its offer at minus $1.30 Tuesday.
A trader reported buying 5,000 barrels-per-day of Line 63 crude at 70 cents over Buena Vista crude.
Kern River crude prices remained flat after California oil companies raised their postings Monday. The heavy grade average price stood $15.32/15.42 a barrel.
Wilmington, an ashphalt crude, remained $17.17/17.27, but one trader said the grade could fall because some major buyers might decline to take it this month.
